action.recommendation: Do not administer for hypersensitivity to pembrolizumab or its excipients.

Urgent consultant risk–benefit review before dosing: avoid in pregnancy unless clinical need requires treatment. For breastfeeding, decide whether to stop breastfeeding or pembrolizumab, balancing benefits and infant risk.
Serious autoimmune disease is a source caution: consultant assessment is needed before dosing.
Clinically significant infection is a source caution: consultant assessment is needed before dosing.
Untreated brain metastases is a source caution: consultant assessment is needed before dosing.
Previous interstitial lung disease is a source caution: consultant assessment is needed before dosing.
Systemic steroid dose >10 mg/day prednisolone equivalent is a caution; review indication, immune suppression and taper. Inhaled/topical steroids are not counted.
Apply current NCCP PD-1/PD-L1 retreatment guidance and confirm indication-specific eligibility; previous exposure is not encoded as a universal absolute contraindication.
Review blood-count abnormalities clinically. The monotherapy source gives no automatic numerical ANC or platelet hold threshold.
Performance status is outside the source ECOG 0–1 eligibility for this indication.
Performance status is outside the source ECOG 0–2 eligibility for this indication.
Select the exact indication: lung, melanoma and Hodgkin source eligibility is ECOG 0–1; other listed indications generally allow 0–2.
First-line metastatic monotherapy requires validated PD-L1 TPS ≥50%.
Confirm validated PD-L1 testing for first-line metastatic NSCLC.
EGFR mutation or ALK translocation is outside this first-line metastatic monotherapy indication.
Confirm stage IV metastatic NSCLC for this first-line indication.
This source lung monotherapy indication is first-line metastatic treatment.

Adjuvant NSCLC requires complete resection, prior platinum chemotherapy and high recurrence-risk/stage IB–IIIA AJCC7 criteria. Reconcile the unmet criterion; confirm access because NCCP lists reimbursement N/A.

Adjuvant NSCLC requires complete resection, prior platinum chemotherapy and high recurrence-risk/stage IB–IIIA AJCC7 criteria. Reconcile the unmet criterion; confirm access because NCCP lists reimbursement N/A.

Adjuvant NSCLC requires complete resection, prior platinum chemotherapy and high recurrence-risk/stage IB–IIIA AJCC7 criteria. Reconcile the unmet criterion; confirm access because NCCP lists reimbursement N/A.

Cisplatin-ineligible urothelial indication table requires CPS ≥10 while eligibility text says >10. CPS below 10 fails; exactly 10 requires consultant/pharmacy source reconciliation, not automatic clearance.
Withhold for grade 2 immune pneumonitis; investigate and manage before considering restart.
Permanently discontinue for grade 3–4 or recurrent grade 2 pneumonitis.
Withhold for grade 2–3 immune colitis; establish cause and treat.
Permanently discontinue for grade 4 or recurrent grade 3 colitis.

In immune nephritis, creatinine >1.5 to ≤3×ULN requires withholding. Confirm ULN basis and investigate other renal causes. This action requires clinician-assessed immune attribution after evaluation of alternative causes.

Immune nephritis with creatinine >3×ULN requires permanent discontinuation; this is not a chronic renal impairment dose rule. This action requires clinician-assessed immune attribution after evaluation of alternative causes.
Withhold for immune hepatitis: AST/ALT >3 to ≤5×ULN or bilirubin >1.5 to ≤3×ULN. This action requires clinician-assessed immune attribution after evaluation of alternative causes.
Permanently discontinue for immune hepatitis with AST/ALT >5×ULN or bilirubin >3×ULN. This action requires clinician-assessed immune attribution after evaluation of alternative causes.

With liver metastases and baseline grade 2 AST/ALT elevation, a ≥50% rise persisting ≥1 week requires permanent discontinuation for hepatitis. This action requires clinician-assessed immune attribution after evaluation of alternative causes.
Withhold for grade 3 immune skin toxicity or suspected SJS/TEN; urgent specialist assessment.
Permanently discontinue for grade 4 skin toxicity or confirmed SJS/TEN.
Permanently discontinue for grade 3–4 myocarditis, encephalitis or Guillain–Barré syndrome.
Withhold for other grade 2–3 immune toxicity according to its type; use a specific Table 1 pathway when applicable.
Permanently discontinue for other grade 4 or recurrent grade 3 immune toxicity without a specific Table 1 exception. Controlled endocrinopathy follows its separate pathway.
Permanently discontinue for a grade 3–4 infusion reaction and manage immediately.
Withhold and urgently assess suspected myocarditis or serious neurological immune toxicity; determine named grade and apply permanent-stop criteria if confirmed.

Withhold uncontrolled adrenal insufficiency/hypophysitis, severe hyperthyroidism or immune diabetes with severe hyperglycaemia/DKA. Stabilise with specialist care; grade 2 adrenal/hypophysitis is held until controlled by hormone replacement.
Withhold for type 1 diabetes with glucose >13.9 mmol/L; urgently assess for ketoacidosis. This threshold is not a generic rule for all hyperglycaemia.
Withhold and arrange urgent hospital assessment for type 1 diabetes with ketoacidosis.
Hypothyroidism may be managed with hormone replacement without interrupting pembrolizumab. This only addresses the thyroid domain and does not clear the whole regimen.

After grade 3–4 endocrinopathy has improved to ≤grade 2 and is controlled with hormone replacement, continuation may be considered after steroid taper when needed. Consultant approval is required; do not apply an automatic generic grade 4 stop.
Discontinue if the source conditions for continuation after severe endocrinopathy are not met; specialist review must establish the ongoing plan.

Permanently discontinue if treatment-related toxicity has not recovered to grade 0–1 by 12 weeks after the last dose or toxicity steroids cannot taper to ≤10 mg/day prednisolone equivalent within 12 weeks. Reconcile specific endocrine exceptions before selecting this condition.
NCCP Table 2 recommends no renal dose adjustment; none is expected for haemodialysis. This does not override active immune-nephritis or other toxicity holds.
No adjustment is needed for mild hepatic impairment; no adjustment is expected for moderate/severe impairment. This does not override active immune-hepatitis rules; review clinical context.
Adjuvant melanoma, RCC and NSCLC have a maximum 12-month course. Confirm completion and do not automatically continue beyond the source duration.
At 24 months, consider discontinuation if there is sustained response and no progression; ongoing treatment may be appropriate. This is an individual decision, not a mandatory fixed cap.

action.recommendation: Abnormal liver result crosses an immune-toxicity table threshold, but immune causality has not been established. Obtain prompt clinical assessment, investigate alternative causes and document the treatment decision. Do not administer automatically or apply permanent immune-toxicity discontinuation from an isolated laboratory result. No dose reduction is calculated.

action.recommendation: Abnormal renal result crosses an immune-toxicity table threshold, but immune causality has not been established. Obtain prompt clinical assessment, investigate alternative causes and document the treatment decision. Do not administer automatically or apply permanent immune-toxicity discontinuation from an isolated laboratory result. No dose reduction is calculated.
The NCCP colorectal indication is for adults. Confirm the appropriate protocol/access route before treatment.
This NCCP colorectal indication is metastatic disease. Nonmetastatic, neoadjuvant or adjuvant use requires a separate treatment/access decision.

This NCCP colorectal indication is first-line treatment. The broader EMA previously-treated indication does not establish eligibility or reimbursement under this NCCP regimen; obtain consultant/pharmacy review.
Confirm histological colorectal diagnosis before treatment under this indication.
Confirm MSI-H or dMMR using a validated test. PD-L1 expression is not a substitute for the colorectal biomarker requirement.

This NCCP colorectal indication requires MSI-H or dMMR. MSS/pMMR or an unknown/indeterminate result does not establish eligibility; clarify the result and treatment plan before prescribing. A PD-L1 result cannot replace MSI/MMR testing.

requirement: 200 mg q21 or400mg q42 IV30minutes, no dose reduction
